  "relation": "DIVERGENT",
  "consensus_summary": "Consensus holds no single settled meaning but centers primarily on the moon as the Church (or people of God) reflecting Christ’s light as the lesser light, or as a cosmic sign of eschatological judgment (darkened/turned to blood); frequent alternatives include appointed seasons, Marian symbolism, mutability, and matriarchal/Israel figures.",
  "book_summary": "The moon is the faithful witness—the Son—who has no light of His own but reflects the Father’s, the lesser light that rules the night and marks appointed times.",
  "consensus_core_identification": "Church reflecting Christ (or cosmic judgment portent)",
  "book_core_identification": "the Son (Christ as faithful witness reflecting the Father)",
  "core_relation": "CONTRADICTS",
  "extension_relation": "DIFFERENT_REFERENT",
  "boundary_disagreement": "Book reassigns the reflected-light/lesser-light/faithful-witness imagery from the Church (or creation-order sign) to the Son himself, thereby excluding the consensus’s primary ecclesial (and judgment) cases from the core slot.",
  "material_contradiction": "Consensus primary (Church as reflector of Christ) and book (Son as reflector of Father) cannot both hold as the moon’s core identification in the same allegorical sense; accepting the book replaces the consensus referent.",
  "rationale": "Minimum cores are Church/judgment-sign versus the Son. The book preserves the ‘reflected lesser light’ language but swaps the identity of the reflector (and the light-source) for a different personal referent, requiring rejection of the standard ecclesial reading that the consensus (and the book’s own common-view note) treats as primary. No listed alternative equates the moon with the Son.",
  "citation_support": "PARTIAL",
  "strongest_objection": "Traditional allegory pairs sun=Christ / moon=Church; reassigning the moon to Christ severs that pairing and rests on an associative ‘faithful witness’ parallel rather than an explicit scriptural equation.",
  "confidence": "high"
}
